files.why: The person's page: reasons the run is theirs (the 0.5 GB and 3 GB figures disagree, under both), pre-flight, the teed command with the artifacts folder made first and the console set to UTF-8, a table of endings, the record fields for criteria 1-4, the Q-261 reconciliation with the same-session floor and the single rule for the code-363 count, what to commit, and a result table.
Two sentences beside the command: use pwsh with -Root C:\ because the cmd.exe form arrives as C:" and stops with nothing written, and a pointer to the SL-107 page.

The settled counts-only rule over the committed record, patterns widened to a closed grammar (any slash, any backslash that is not a JSON quote or code-unit escape, the u005c and u002f spellings, the path key).
Corpus closing the class of path spellings without a drive letter: 44 rows, each with the first draft's hit count.
Reads the patterns from fitness.yaml, applies them to every corpus row, checks the writer and the rule agree, and applies the rule to any record on this machine.

Cases C-001 to C-006: the cmd.exe form, the seams doc, the SL-107 doc (including the UTF-8 line and the single code-363 rule), W-001 over D:\, over the tree holding the layer store, and over the fsa-guard-tests fixtures.
Pins O-016: the real Planting plants S83-S86 and P36 over an existing record and restores its bytes, creates and removes it when absent, and still marks a non-awaited existing file PLANT-BROKEN.

load_awaiting, check_clean and describe_unmatched let a rule listed under awaiting_file match no file while its file is absent; Planting._create plants over an existing awaiting file and restore() writes its bytes back.
awaiting_file entry, rows S83-S86 and P36, and the note's counts and history (the note names the Python test that pins the overwrite).
Design record kept in step: the rule's patterns, and would_force_resynthesis false with the 0.5 GB / 3 GB disagreement kept as a recorded fact.

M2 built: a same-session floor of three bounded W-001 runs (C:/Windows, C:/ProgramData, the user's Temp) with the records copied to anchor-windows.json, anchor-programdata.json and anchor-temp.json, the sum as the floor, the remainder named, and the old Layers share stated as unmeasurable.

m1 closed as a class with a closed grammar: '/' ; any backslash not followed by a quote or u, plus the u005c and u002f escapes; the path key kept. Corpus tests/bugs/SL-107-RecordPathRuleCorpus.json has 44 rows over drive-letter, row-key, UNC, relative, variable-rooted, hand-typed, escaped-separator, residual and record families; the first draft's patterns fail 21 of them, and the writer and the rule agree on every writer row.

m2 built through the repo's harness so the engine's own Fitness runs: plants.json rows S83-S86 fire and P36 (a whole real record) stays quiet, AS-RECORDED with 0 strays. With the slash pattern removed the harness exits 1.

The design record has would_force_resynthesis false with the 0.5 GB / 3 GB disagreement kept as a recorded fact; the doc's reason section does not rest on 0.5 GB and states the figures disagree and the run is the person's under both. WindowCases.ps1 is untouched and SL-089-seams.md has only the two planned sentences.
obligations.not_mutable: A flag in the engine's exported design record (overwritten from the engine store on refresh, Q-106) and a paragraph of the doc; the doc's reason section is checked by case C-003.

obligations.how: Planting._create plants over an existing file listed under awaiting_file: it records the bytes in saved and manifest, does not add the file to created, and restore() writes them back and checks the SHA-256. The previous proof (RuleCases C-008 bite) pushed C-008 past 120 s, so it was replaced by tests/bugs/SL-107-HarnessPlantsOverRecord.Tests.py: the real Planting on the real rows S83-S86 and P36, on a tiny tree, 0.3 s. Over an existing record every row is planted, not PLANT-BROKEN, and the record's bytes are back; with no record it is created and removed; a non-awaited existing file is still PLANT-BROKEN. Also run once as the finding asked, with a record present at the path in the worktree (temporary, removed): harness.py --only S83,S84,S85,S86,P36 exited 0, 5 AS-RECORDED, 0 strays, the record restored byte for byte. RuleCases C-008 is back to its earlier 80 s and passes.

deviations: The design said change no code. The engine-appended counts-only rule matches no file until the person commits the record, and the repo's harness refused a clean baseline with an unmatched rule (exit 2). I added the awaiting_file allowance to the harness, and, per review M1, the plant rows plant over the record once it exists.

m1's literal fix was widened to a closed grammar (any slash, any backslash that is not a JSON quote or code-unit escape, the u005c and u002f spellings): a path typed with single backslashes is valid JSON and the pair pattern misses it.
m2 (the engine's Fitness over the rule) was built as harness plant rows S83-S86 and P36 rather than as a validate-time step; the owed cases C-001 to C-006 are runnable scripts in tests/bugs.

O-016's pin is a Python unit test of the real Planting and rows, not a RuleCases case: a RuleCases bite took C-008 to 127 s, past the 120 s a reproduction is allowed, and a new case function would also need a census row. The bite was removed; C-008 is 80 s again.
The design record .taad/slices/SL-107/design-slice-1.json was edited as the builder instruction required; it is an engine export and may be overwritten (Q-106).

No workaround, setting or notice was added: the run depends on the existing wcifs-layer-store entry. Both switch positions and the on-screen notice are covered by the existing cases X-004 and X-005, which were run and passed.

follow_ups: Once the person's record is committed, the awaiting_file entry in plants.json can be dropped; the harness works either way.
If the person's run ends TIMEOUT, raise the 1,200 literal in Invoke-HookedRun 'rows' inside Test-W001 (then run WindowMutants -Mutant All per Q-114).
Expose the refused-then-listed count (LastAccessAsked minus Kept minus Unreadable.Count, per U-102) in the report so a W-001 record can show the roughly 306,000 context figure.
